subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX, concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from my side and the next steps we discussed. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- Tail latency spikes during peak trading hours cause degraded streaming UX for end users (partial results arrive inconsistently).
- Current hosts (mix of OpenAI hosted + small on-prem LLMs) are showing p95 latency > 1s for short chat requests and > 2s for some longer streaming flows at peak.
- No consistent shaping between initial-token latency and sustained stream delta, makes UI jittery.
- Concurrency at peak: ~300 concurrent active users, spikes up to ~450 for short windows.

Current stack
- Frontend: React app with streaming client, relies on a backend inference proxy.
- Backend: mix of OpenAI API (primary) + self-hosted instances (batching attempted at app layer).
- Auth/data flow: customer metadata + embeddings stored in Finly infra, inference requests pass PII filters at proxy.

Success criteria (what Finly needs to see to consider a pilot)
- p95 (chat generation initial token) <= 200ms for short prompts (<64 tokens).
- sustained streaming consistency: initial token < 200ms and per-chunk delta <= 150ms under target concurrency.
- Ability to sustain 300 concurrent active sessions (with headroom to 500) without p95 degradation >20% vs baseline.
- No data exfiltration; turnkey VPC/private option for pilot if needed.

Key risks called out
- Mixed model topology and fallback to OpenAI during spikes (we need to understand fallback behavior).
- Current instrumentation gaps: no clear token-distribution histogram and incomplete p95 tracing across proxy.

Attachments (from Finly): finly-arch-diagram.pdf (requested)

Next steps (agreed)
1) Finly to share current request QPS and a token-length distribution (bins for 0-64, 65-256, 257-1024) — Samir to send by EOD Thu.
2) Redwood to propose a tech deep-dive to align on streaming protocol and kernel expectations (Aditya to lead) — propose Wed/Thu next week.
3) Exchange draft mutual action plan + pilot scope (Mutual Action Plan attached) — Marissa will send a templated MAP.
4) If agreed, set up a short on-site bench test (or private VPC pilot) to validate p95 targets on representative traffic.

If that all looks right I'll schedule the deep-dive and send the MAP template.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.coole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Jia Chen <jia.chen@finly.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 17:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Thanks Marissa — this is a good summary and matches what we heard internally. A couple clarifications and I'll attach the architecture diagram you requested.

Clarifications:
- Peak concurrency: our telemetry shows 275 sustained concurrent users during normal peak, with daily spikes up to ~480 for short promo-driven windows.
- Token distribution (rough): ~55% <64 tokens, ~30% 65-256, ~15% >256.
- Current p95 numbers (observed last week): 1) short-chat p95 (initial token) ~ 1.1s, 2) streaming delta p95 ~ 700ms, 3) embedding p95 ~ 180ms.

Constraints and notes:
- We have contractual constraints that prevent sending raw customer data to third-party hosted models without an approved private deployment path.
- We can share anonymized traffic traces and a sanitized example request set.

Attachment: finly-arch-diagram.pdf (schema diagram)

Happy to move forward on the deep-dive — Wed/Thu next week both OK for Jia and me.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Finly
samir.patel@finly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Appreciate the detail, Samir — that's really helpful. Two quick asks before the tech deep-dive so we can size the pilot accurately: 

1) Can you export a 24-hour sample of request metadata (timestamps, request type, token_count, success/failure, region) with PII stripped? A CSV is fine.
2) Do you have a sample of the client streaming behavior (chunk size, interval) so we can match the streaming chunking in our bench test?

I'll attach a starter Mutual Action Plan (CSV) that outlines scope, timelines, and responsibilities — see attached: mutual-action-plan-Finly.csv.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (30-45m):
- 10m: Finly current infra & constraints (Samir/Jia)
- 10m: Redwood runtime + streaming model expectations (Aditya)
- 10m: Bench test design and success criteria (Marissa/Rishi)
- 5m: Logistics / pilot next steps

Aditya — can you propose two slots on Wed/Thu next week (PDT) and confirm if we want Redwood infra or a private VPC pilot first?

Thanks — attaching MAP: mutual-action-plan-Finly.csv

Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.inference>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finly.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Thanks — I can run the deep-dive. Proposed slots (PDT):
- Wed 13 May 2026 10:00–10:45
- Thu 14 May 2026 14:00–14:45

For the bench test: I recommend starting on Redwood hosted infra (fastest to iterate) and then move to a private VPC pilot if you need guarantees around data residency. For the initial run we'll need:
- 24-hour sanitized request CSV (headers: timestamp, endpoint, token_count, client_chunk_ms, success)
- An example streaming session capture (we can use a small harness to replay chunk timing)
- Preferred SLA/pass-fail: p95 initial token <200ms, streaming chunk delta <150ms at 300 concurrent; if that fails we'll capture profiling and propose quant/kinetic changes.

I'll block both slots tentatively — Samir/Jia let me know which works and I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in and a short runbook.

-Aditya
Senior Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.inference
